instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines "lobbying" as attempting to influence legislative or administrative action "by oral or written communication," enumerating only oral and written modalities (plus preparation/appearances).

A "lobbyist" is an individual employed by or contracting with a principal; a "principal" includes associations, corporations, LLCs, or partnerships, capturing contract/professional lobbyists as well as in-house employees of companies and organizations.
The definitions section does not include a defined term for "public entity"; the statute defines "agency," "business entity," and "principal" but not "public entity."

The statute contains materiality thresholds: principals spending ≤$500/year may file a verified statement exempting them from registration/reporting, and an individual is a lobbyist only if they make lobbying communications on at least 5 days in a reporting period.

Lobbying covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative employees, and "legislative action" explicitly includes the governor's approving/vetoing bills, capturing both legislative and executive (including the governor) branches.

Targets of lobbying include elective state officials (executive), legislative employees (members/officers of legislature and staff), and agency officials (administrative bureaucracy), and "legislative action" covers the governor and agency development of proposals.
Same as row_005: lobbying definition covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials and legislative employees, and legislative action expressly includes the governor's actions.

Same as row_005: the statutory definition covers communications with both legislative employees/elective state officials and agency officials, and "legislative action" explicitly includes the governor.
Same as row_005: lobbying reaches communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative employees, and legislative action includes the governor's approving or vetoing bills.
Same as row_006: targets include legislative branch members and employees, executive branch elective officials (governor named in §13.62(8)), and agency officials (senior bureaucracy/staff).

State agencies must file a statement identifying officers/employees whose duties include attempting to influence legislative action; while elected state, local, tribal officials and legislative employees acting in official capacity are exempt under §13.621(3), agency officials/employees engaged in lobbying must be identified.

The statute applies compensation/expenditure/time thresholds: lobbyists must receive economic consideration (compensation), principal registration is triggered by >$500 expenditures, and the "5 days" test plus 10-hour employee threshold in §13.68(1)(a) reflect time standards applicable to public-employee-type lobbyists registered under §13.695.
